# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 7
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 7

---

*[Thomas comes to the city of a king. A serpent/dragon confesses to killing a young man for lust. Thomas compels the serpent to draw out its own venom.]*

1. And it came to pass after these things that Thomas went on and came to another city. And there he saw a young man lying dead.

2. And they told him that a serpent had killed him. And the woman who was his wife mourned over him greatly and wept.

3. And Thomas had compassion upon her and said to her: "Do not weep, for your Lord Jesus Christ shall raise up your husband for you."

4. And when Thomas had said this, the serpent came out of a hole near that place and said: "You servant of God, why have you come here to lay bare our works and to shame us?"

5. And Thomas said to the serpent: "Tell me, what is it that you have done, and for what reason did you kill this young man?"

6. And the serpent said: "I had seen him with a young woman, and I loved her and I was jealous of him and I killed him."

7. And Thomas said: "Now go and draw out the poison you have injected into him."

8. And the serpent said: "I am not able to do this unless I take back the venom into my own body."

9. And Thomas said: "Then take it back into yourself."

10. And the serpent went and placed his mouth upon the wound where he had bitten the man and sucked out all the poison.

11. And when he had done so, the young man's body swelled up and puffed out, and the serpent swelled up and burst asunder.

12. And the young man rose up healed.

13. And many believed on account of this sign.

14. And Thomas baptized them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.

---
*EMET note: The serpent as a figure of demonic lust and jealousy (here explicitly confessing sexual desire for the woman) connects to the Eden tradition. The serpent's self-destruction — sucking back the venom — is a precise inversion: the weapon of death becomes death.*
